commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[skyrl] Resume Megatron checkpoints saved with CPU optimizer offload (#10715)

Loading a checkpoint into a Megatron policy with `optimizer_cpu_offload:
true` failed with a `KeyError` in Megatron's
`HybridDeviceOptimizer._update_fp32_params_by_new_state`, so no run with
that setting could resume. The Snowball OPD recipe
(`snowball_mopd_ultra_32k.yaml`) uses it: resuming a Snowball 67B
checkpoint through that recipe on main failed in the first 10 seconds of
the policy load.

The method looks up an fp32 copy for every parameter with optimizer
state, but `param_to_fp32_param` holds only parameters that were not
already fp32, and the distributed optimizer passes fp32 main shards
only. Every load runs it, starting with the self-reload in
`DistributedOptimizer.sharded_state_dict(is_loading=True)`, before any
checkpoint file is read. Megatron 0.18.0 through 0.19.2 is affected.
SkyRL now replaces the method with one that skips parameters that have
no separate fp32 copy.

Once the load succeeded, the next save needed tens of GiB more host
memory per rank than a save in a run that never resumed. On Snowball 67B
at 768 GB per learner node, the save after a resume was killed for low
node memory. Restoring offloaded optimizer state makes
`HybridDeviceOptimizer` rebuild its pinned host copies of every
parameter, and PyTorch's caching host allocator keeps the replaced
pinned blocks. `load_checkpoint` now synchronizes and calls
`torch.accelerator.memory.empty_host_cache()` after restoring the
optimizer, as `load_megatron_model_to_gpu` already does. On a
1.6B-parameter Grug MoE at DP=2, this brings the post-resume save's peak
RSS from 31.7 to 28.9 GiB per rank, against 28.8 GiB without a resume.
With it, the Snowball 67B resume at 768 GB per node trains, saves, and
resumes again from that save.

The new GPU test saves an offloaded checkpoint at DP=2, steps again,
reloads, and requires the restored weights to equal the saved ones and
the next step to repeat the step taken after saving, exactly. It also
requires every rank to hold no idle pinned host memory after the load.
It fails with the `KeyError` without the method replacement, and with
174,685,007 idle pinned bytes per rank without the release. It writes
the checkpoint to S3 scratch because Megatron restore reads only
CoreWeave S3 checkpoints.
